candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes large fixed periarticular calcified masses with fluctuance, soft tissue calcifications on imaging, and normal phosphorus (1.7 mg/dL is actually low/normal, consistent with normophosphatemic tumoral calcinosis), along with a childhood-onset condition and African American ethnicity — all hallmarks of Tumoral Calcinosis. Calcinosis Cutis is a related but broader parent category encompassing various forms of soft tissue calcification; it lacks the specific anatomical pattern (large periarticular tumoral deposits), the distinct clinical entity designation, and the normophosphatemic subtype specification. The necrosis component is present in both but does not resolve the subtype gap.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Calcinosis Cutis is a broader/related category of soft tissue calcification affecting skin and subcutaneous tissue; it does not specify the tumoral calcinosis subtype (large periarticular calcium deposits) nor the normophosphatemic subtype required by the benchmark

case_quality_flags: Phosphorus of 1.7 mg/dL is at the low end of normal/mildly depressed, consistent with normophosphatemic tumoral calcinosis rather than hyperphosphatemic subtype
Childhood-onset condition at age 8 in an African American male from West Africa strongly supports familial normophosphatemic tumoral calcinosis
